feedback.problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{5}^{n}(x-4)^{n}}{n!}=5(x-4)+\frac{{5}^{2}(x-4)^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{5}^{3}(x-4)^{3}}{3!}+⋯\,.
$$

$R=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{5}^{n}(x-4)^{n}}{n!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{\frac{{5}^{n+1}(x-4)^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}}{\frac{{5}^{n}(x-4)^{n}}{n!}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{5}^{n+1}(x-4)^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}\cdot \frac{n!}{{5}^{n}(x-4)^{n}}| \\  & =5|x-4|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{n+1} \\  & =5|x-4|\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$  Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty .$
